public.prompt: A Vue 3 composable starts a preview session containing several watchers, computed values, and one WebSocket. A component can start and stop multiple sessions without unmounting. Stopping a session must dispose its complete reactive graph and socket together. Which ownership model fits?

options.label: Create an `effectScope`, build the session inside `scope.run`, register socket closure with `onScopeDispose`, and call `scope.stop`.
Store the latest watch stop handle, call it when the session ends, and let computed values and the socket expire independently.
Create the session effects in component setup and rely on `onUnmounted` to close every socket after the component eventually leaves.

optionRationales.explanation: The effect scope captures every reactive effect created for one session, and its disposal callback brings the non-reactive socket into the same stop boundary.
Stopping one remembered watcher leaves the other session effects active and gives the socket no deterministic ownership or teardown point.
optionRationales.plausibility: Each Vue watch call returns a handle that can stop that individual watcher.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: Every effect and the socket created by the session must share one disposal boundary.

optionRationales.explanation: Component unmount occurs later than a session stop, so replaced sessions continue reacting and keep their sockets open inside the still-mounted component.
optionRationales.plausibility: Effects created synchronously in setup are normally stopped when their owner component unmounts.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: A preview session can end while the component that launched it remains mounted.

answerProof.summary: An effect scope gives each restartable preview session its own reactive lifetime, while onScopeDispose attaches WebSocket cleanup to the same explicit stop operation.
decisiveConstraints: One component can own several sequential session lifetimes.
All watchers and computed effects from an ended session must stop together.
The WebSocket requires non-reactive cleanup at the same boundary.

claims.statement: Vue effectScope captures computed values and watchers created inside its run callback so `scope.stop()` can dispose them together.
Vue onScopeDispose registers a callback that runs when the current active effect scope is stopped.
